text:
**For a full recharge in one day, plan on roughly 300-400 W of panels. If you can wait a day and a half, 200 W is enough.**

**The math**

Daily solar energy = panel watts × peak sun hours × about 0.7-0.75. The multiplier covers heat, panel angle, and charge-controller losses ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge)).

Panel watts for a one-day recharge of 1,000 Wh ([Power Station Runtime Calculator](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)):

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts |
|---|---|
| 3 | ~450 W |
| 4 | ~340 W |
| 5 | ~270 W |
| 6 | ~230 W |

- **200 W panel:** At 4.5 sun hours and 70% efficiency, it yields about 630 Wh/day, so a 1,000 Wh station takes about 1.5 days ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/), [Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station)).
- **400 W panel:** It yields about 1,260 Wh/day, enough for a one-day refill.
- **Winter:** In a northern winter (about 2 sun hours), a one-day refill could take 700 W or more ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

**Check before you buy**
- **Solar input limit:** Your station caps how many watts it accepts. Many 1,000 Wh units take 200-800 W, and panels beyond the cap add nothing on a clear day.
- **Voltage:** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside your station's input voltage window. Exceeding it can damage the charge controller, and panels wired in series add their voltages.
- **Connector:** Panels usually have MC4 connectors, while stations often use XT60 or DC barrel plugs, so you may need an adapter.
- **Charging while running loads:** If you're also using the station, the net recharge is slower.

**One option for the 400 W case**

The [ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W foldable panel](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel) is listed at $299, or $269.10 with code ALLPOWERS26, which Dealectric says expires 2026-12-30. That's an affiliate link, so Dealectric is paid if you buy. Its specs are:
- 37.4 V working voltage and 45.3 V open-circuit voltage.
- MC4 connectors, with XT60 and DC adapters included.
- 18.5 kg, which is heavy for a folding panel.

Its voltage is too high for stations with a low input window, such as the Tenergy T320 (5-24 V) and the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 (12-28 V). If you tell me your station model, I can help check its limits and compatibility.
